description:
AgentHub manages the MCP servers and skills of the coding agents built into Xcode — Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity — from a single window.

Each agent keeps its configuration in its own file, in its own format: JSON for Claude Code and Antigravity, TOML for Codex. AgentHub reads all three, shows them side by side, and writes each one back in the format that agent expects, leaving the rest of the file untouched.

MCP SERVERS
• Add and edit servers over standard I/O or HTTP.
• Turn a server off without deleting it. It is stashed in whichever disabled list that agent understands, and comes back exactly as it was.
• Check an HTTP server with Test Connection, which performs an MCP initialize handshake and reports the name the server answers with.
• Copy servers to another agent, written in that agent's own format.

SKILLS
• Browse the skills each agent has installed.
• Compose the YAML frontmatter with a form rather than a text editor: dedicated fields for name, description and allowed-tools, and a key/value table for anything else.
• Edit an existing SKILL.md through the same form. A file carrying YAML the form cannot represent opens as raw Markdown instead, so nothing is rewritten behind your back.
• Import a skill folder as a copy, or link to it where it already lives. A linked skill stays one folder: keep it in a dotfiles repo, edit it there or here, and every agent linked to it sees the change.
• Copy a skill to another agent — as a link, if that is what it was.

Every write backs up the file it touches first.

AgentHub only reads and writes the agent configuration folder that you grant it access to on first launch. It does not modify Xcode itself.

AgentHub is open source, released under the Apache License 2.0.

AgentHub is an independent developer utility. It is not made by Apple, and it is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Apple Inc. Xcode is a trademark of Apple Inc.
promotionalText: One window for the MCP servers and skills of every coding agent in Xcode.
